title: Fix launcher session resume and first-run auth

history.detail:
FAIL: FAIL — Round 1. Audited commit 9589518 against the current (amended) sprint file, including 1a-1c, 5a, 6a-6b.

Most of this sprint is right. The UUIDv5 implementation is textbook-correct (SHA-1 over namespace+name bytes, version nibble forced to 5, variant to 10xx, node:crypto only, package.json untouched). state.js is fully deleted with no surviving reference, FAST_FAILURE_MS is gone, .gitignore no longer mentions .claude-launcher/. --resume receives only the UUID; the display name is confined to --name. No JSON parsing on the auth path. The generation scheme's logic is sound in the abstract and the restart round trip is genuinely tested. The 35-test suite passes. The kids also correctly kept the out-of-scope .vscode/settings.json change out of the commit.

I independently verified the assumption Req 6 rests on, which nobody had confirmed: `claude auth status` exits 0 logged in and exits 1 logged out (tested with an isolated CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR, real login untouched). Req 6a's exit-code-only design is correct. I also confirmed an unrecognised subcommand on this CLI exits 0 rather than non-zero, so an older CLI lacking `auth status` proceeds rather than blocking — Req 6b's named case fails safe.

BLOCKER — sessionsDir() mis-derives every repo path containing a space, and probably more. session.js:71 replaces only [\\/]. The real Claude CLI also collapses spaces to '-'. Proven against this machine's own session directories: /Users/chrishobbs/Programming/Licenseprofessor Edits and fixes encodes to -Users-chrishobbs-Programming-Licenseprofessor-Edits-and-fixes on disk, while sessionsDir() produces '...-Programming-Licenseprofessor Edits and fixes', which does not exist. Seven directories under this user's own ~/Programming contain spaces.

This is not a graceful degradation to always-fresh. It is worse, and it breaks the sprint's own load-bearing claim:
- highestExistingGeneration() sees no files, so every launch returns resume:false at generation 0.
- run-role.js then passes --session-id <generation-0 uuid> on every single launch, while that .jsonl already exists in the real directory the code cannot see.
- That is a direct violation of Req 1c. The structural guarantee is real, but it is conditional on sessionsDir() being correct, and it is not. The struck-through in-use-ID risk is therefore live again, invoked on every launch.
- Every launch also mints a new orphan .jsonl — the exact symptom (56 orphans) this sprint exists to stop, and it fails the Windows acceptance criterion "no new orphan .jsonl files accumulate per launch".

Answering Dev Team 1's direct question about Req 1c: your reading of resolveSession() is correct. Restart at highest+1 never collides, the highest-not-first-gap choice is right, and the bounded fallback is fine. The flaw is not in that function. It is one layer down, in the path derivation every existsSync() call depends on.

Severity is raised by where this lands. The sprint file names Windows path encoding as the single most likely way this fix passes QA1 and still fails on Windows. Windows home directories routinely contain a space (C:\Users\Chris Hobbs\...). This would have shipped straight into the sprint's own top risk.

MAJOR — the Windows test asserts an unverified guess as if it were coverage. launcher_test.js:133-139 asserts C:\Users\... encodes to 'C:-Users-...', keeping the drive-letter colon verbatim. Nothing verifies that. Given the CLI demonstrably rewrites spaces, it very likely rewrites ':' and '.' too. A test that hardcodes the implementation's own assumption passes forever and proves nothing, which is why both path tests went green over a broken derivation. Determine the CLI's actual encoding rule empirically (a throwaway repo whose path contains a space, a dot, and on Windows a drive letter — check what directory actually appears under ~/.claude/projects), implement that rule, and write the tests against the observed encoding rather than the assumed one.

MINOR — auth.js classify() falls through to 'unauthenticated' as its default. Its own comment says anything short of a clean, completed non-zero exit must not block, but the code only checks probe.error and probe.signal explicitly. A probe.status that is null or undefined for any other reason lands on block, which is the one direction Req 6b says must never happen by accident. Make the final branch assert a completed numeric non-zero status and treat everything else as inconclusive.

MINOR — README overstates the preflight: "refuses to start any role session until this is done" contradicts Req 6b's inconclusive-proceeds branch. README also describes the session ID as derived from (role, repo path), dropping the generation that 1a added. Bring both in line with what the code actually does.

Required before re-audit: fix the derivation against the CLI's real encoding rule, replace both path tests with assertions based on observed behaviour (including a space in the path), tighten classify()'s default, correct the two README statements. Then re-run /sprint-qa1 1. The Windows acceptance gate still belongs to the user and is unaffected by this verdict.
